_readme: ONE hand-maintained map from a Simfly canonical product id to the
supplier SKU on each digital supplier. Routing below is EXPLICIT —
an entry always wins; nothing is name-matched to decide WHERE an
order is placed.
products.<canonicalId> = {
"prodseller": "<prodSeller product id> or null",
"eklas":      "<eklas product id> or null",
"locked":     true   // optional: never fall back to the other supplier
both ids set  -> price compare: the cheaper IN STOCK supplier wins,
and checkout falls back to the other one if the
winner runs out / is broke / is not configured
prodseller only (or no entry at all) -> ProdSeller, exactly as before
prodseller: null + eklas set -> Eklas-only shelf item (canonical id = the key)
EVERY Eklas product is listed on the shelf, entry or no entry:
• an Eklas item whose polished shelf name matches one already listed
is NOT shown twice — it is linked as that row's alternate, so the
price compare and the fallback still use it
• a unique Eklas item gets its own row, canonical id = "eklas:<sku>"
• the same product Eklas lists twice under one name appears once
Top level "locked": [canonicalId, …] does the same thing per product.
Default supplier for anything unmapped: "default".
Hand-pinned example (Google Gemini): ProdSeller is the primary —
it sells at 0.60 USD vs Eklas 0.94 — so it wins today and keeps
winning while Eklas stays dearer; the entry links the two SKUs so
ONE shelf row is shown and the compare runs automatically.
Add "locked": true if Gemini should never move to Eklas at all.
